description.text: Zions Bancorporation, National Association (“Zions Bancorporation, N.A.,” “the Bank,” “we,” “our,” “us”) is a bank headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, with annual net revenue (net interest income and noninterest income) of $3.4 billion in 2025, and total assets of approximately $89 billion at December 31, 2025. We provide a wide range of banking products and related services, primarily in 11 Western states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming. At December 31, 2025, we had more than one million customers, served through 407 branches and various online, mobile, and digital channels, and we had 9,195 full-time equivalent employees. Our operations are organized principally through seven separately managed, geographically defined bank divisions, which we refer to as “affiliates,” or “affiliate banks,” each operating under its own local brand and management team: Zions Bank; California Bank & Trust (“CB&T”); Amegy Bank (“Amegy”); National Bank of Arizona (“NBAZ”); Nevada State Bank (“NSB”); Vectra Bank Colorado (“Vectra”); and The Commerce Bank of ZIONS BANCORPORATION, NATIONAL ASSOCIATION AND SUBSIDIARIES Washington (“TCBW”), which also operates as The Commerce Bank of Oregon in Oregon. These affiliate banks constitute our primary operating segments.

about.description_short: Zions Bancorporation, N.A. is one of the nation's premier financial services companies with approximately $89 billion of total assets at December 31, 2025, and annual net revenue of $3.4 billion in 2025. Zions operates under local management teams and distinct brands in 11 western states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming. The Bank is a consistent recipient of national and state-wide customer survey awards in small- and middle-market banking, as well as a leader in public finance advisory services and Small Business Administration lending. In addition, Zions is included in the S&P MidCap 400 and NASDAQ Financial 100 indices. Investor information and links to local banking brands can be accessed at www.zionsbancorporation.com.

analysis_md:
# ZION — Zions Bancorporation, National Association

Pass-1 run, 2026-10-20. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
A Western US regional bank holding company (SIC 6021, National Commercial Banks; fundamentals.json profile): seven local bank brands (Zions Bank, California Bank & Trust, Nevada State Bank, etc.) with local management across 11 western states, serving retail, small-business and middle-market commercial customers. Revenue is ~90% net interest income; total assets $88.99B, equity $7.18B at FY2025 (financials_history.csv). Market cap $9.505B at $64.59 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

Latest print (Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-19, per earnings coverage): net earnings to common $262M, diluted EPS $1.78 vs $1.48 a year earlier; revenue $893M, +2.4% YoY; taxable-equivalent NII $684M, +2% YoY; NIM 3.23%, down 4bp sequentially on higher deposit costs; net charge-offs 2bp of average loans; average customer deposits +8.8% annualized. Management guided Q3 2027 NII +8% to +12% versus Q3 2026, assuming three rate increases through June 2027.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,073M; capex $121.0M (rollup: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, key_numbers.md); SBC $35M (a real cost, small at a bank).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $917.0M = $6.23/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $917.0M; latest FY OE/share $6.23).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC per the CSV): $899M — numerically close to the conservative figure in FY2025, but for a bank both are artefacts of balance-sheet flows, not measures of distributable earnings (see SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH below).
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but the per-share series is flow noise: FY2021 $2.47, FY2022 $8.32, FY2023 $5.00, FY2024 $6.92, FY2025 $6.23 (financials_history.csv).
- The earnings record the OCF series should be judged against: diluted EPS FY2023 $4.35, FY2024 $4.95, FY2025 $6.01 (fundamentals.json); net income FY2025 $899M; ROE 12.5% in FY2025, 12.0–18.5% over FY2022–25; ROA ~1.0%.

**Base used = the engine's normalized base, median of the last 3 FY OE/share = $6.23/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; latest FY and normalized are both $6.23 in key_numbers.md).

**TTM rejected — both bases recorded side by side (Q5 checkability rule):** ttm.py built a clean TTM through Q2 2026 (ttm.json, no warnings): OCF FY $1,073M − prior YTD $117M + current YTD $845M = TTM $1,801M; capex TTM $121M; SBC TTM $36M; shares 146,621,000 → **TTM OE $1,644M = $11.21/share**. Run through the identical scenario set (moat 4, probs 15/30/30/15/10), that base prints **weighted IRR 21.65%, Tier A, IV@15 $100.36**. The median base prints **weighted IRR 13.34%, Tier C by numbers, IV@15 $55.78**. The TTM is rejected because the distorting line is operating cash flow itself: H1 2026 YTD OCF of $845M versus H1 2025's $117M is a **$728M half-year swing** in a bank's balance-sheet flows (loans held for sale, deposit and other operating asset/liability movements), not a change in earnings power — over the same window TTM net income was $1,171M (fundamentals.json), and even that contains Q2 2026's one-off equity securities gain (quarter net income $453M, reported EPS $3.05 versus $1.74 adjusted). A base that flips the verdict from C to A on an OCF swing is the misfit artifact, not information.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate
Justification: relationship-driven Western regional bank — seven local brands with local management, multi-generational middle-market relationships and SBA / public-finance niches give real deposit stickiness, but there is no structural cost or scale advantage versus the national banks, NIM is hostage to the rate cycle and deposit competition, and returns are ordinary bank returns. Evidence: fundamentals.json's `roic_proxy` is not computable for this filer (operating income is not filed — the series is null), so the return evidence is ROE 12.5% (FY2025), 12.0–18.5% across FY2022–25, and ROA ~0.8–1.0% — respectable bank returns earned on a leveraged balance sheet, not evidence of a wide moat. Gross margin is not a meaningful bank metric and fundamentals.json does not file one.
- FOR: seven local bank brands with local management across 11 western states — deep, often multi-generational middle-market relationships and switching costs; stable core deposit franchise in faster-growing Western markets (average customer deposits +8.8% annualized in Q3 2026, funding reduced wholesale borrowings); specialist niches with reputation — SBA lending and public finance advisory; disciplined credit culture (Q3 2026 net charge-offs 2bp of average loans, criticized/classified balances falling).
- AGAINST: no scale or technology advantage versus the national banks, and deposit pricing competition compresses NIM (3.23% in Q3 2026, −4bp sequentially); earnings are rate-cycle and credit-cycle hostages — revenue CAGR only ~4.4% over five years and ~90% of revenue is net interest income; Western commercial real estate and regional-economy concentration; heavier post-2023 regional-bank regulatory/liquidity scrutiny, and a $50M fraudulent-loan charge-off in the California operations surfaced in 2025 disclosures.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years (key_numbers.md): growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended start is 5.08% (components in key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 5.65%, rev CAGR 3y 2.24%, latest rev YoY 3.12%, OE/share CAGR 2y 11.61%, share-count adj +0.70%). Against the actual prints — Q3 2026 revenue +2.4% YoY and NII +2% YoY on the low side, management's Q3 2027 NII guide of +8% to +12% on the high side — the 5.1% base start sits defensibly between them, and the 10.1% bull start matches the top of the guided NII range. The 17.1% super-bull start exceeds anything printed or guided; it is a 10%-weighted tail paired with the 1.25 OE multiplier, not a forecast. Probabilities were shifted bear-ward from the 10/25/30/25/10 default to 15/30/30/15/10 per the OE_VOLATILE flag; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $64.59.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -6.9% | 0.75 | $26.55 | 7.32% |
| Bear | 30% | 0.1% | 0.90 | $41.88 | 10.54% |
| Base | 30% | 5.1% | 1.00 | $56.40 | 13.45% |
| Bull | 15% | 10.1% | 1.10 | $75.00 | 16.89% |
| Super bull | 10% | 17.1% | 1.25 | $110.59 | 22.65% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $55.78 (−13.6% vs price), IV@12% $73.96, weighted IRR 13.34%, base-case IRR 13.45%** (key_numbers.md).
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 9.65%, terminal value 18.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.17x, net debt 4.25x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $55.78, 20% at $39.41, 25% at $30.38 — the $64.59 price clears none of them on the numbers base.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 9.6 months ago): the TTM was built with ttm.py and quoted in full above — and rejected with the distorting line named with its number (H1 OCF $845M vs $117M, a $728M swing), with both bases' IRR and tier recorded side by side. The median-of-3-FY base is used.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 years spans >3x — FY2021 $2.47 to FY2022 $8.32 in the CSV): real, and structural for a bank — it is balance-sheet flow noise, not an inflection. Handled by the normalized median base and by widening the bear weight (super bear 15%, bear 30%).
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED**: the only FY2025 cash tag is the combined cash + restricted-cash total, $683M (financials_history.csv), so the engine's net debt of $3.893B is understated by whatever restricted amount is inside it. Balance sheet from the filing (CSV latest row): total assets $88.99B, liabilities $81.81B, equity $7.18B, total debt per the engine's tags $4.576B (long-term $1.472B + short-term borrowings $3.104B). For a bank this net-debt figure is not a leverage measure in any case — deposits, the real funding, are not in the debt tags; capital is (see HIGH_NET_DEBT).
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance sector): the controlling flag.
